title: Q3 Adaptive Dedicated Capacity: Canary Phases, Cost Backstops, and Runbook Enablement
creator: Amelia Park
description:
Goal:
Deliver an end-to-end Q3 roadmap slice that enables predictable and safe autoscale rollouts for Dedicated capacity. Scope includes: a phased canary plan (three wave model), explicit cost backstop definitions and automated enforcement points, a concise on-call and runbook artifact for SRE/operators, and dashboard telemetry to measure rollouts against SLOs and spend guardrails.

Why this is important:
- Customers running Reserved/Dedicated pools require predictable latency and predictable bill impact during scale events.
- Current manual canaries and ad-hoc rollback practices create variability in customer experience and risk unexpected spend.
- Shipping a repeatable, documented canary + cost backstop cadence reduces incident churn and shortens time-to-recover for capacity regressions.

Outcomes (success criteria):
1) Canary plan defined and automated for 3 waves (10%, 40%, 100%) with clear gating metrics.
2) Cost backstop is formalized: per-customer daily spend delta threshold + automated soft-throttle and alerting.
3) Operators have a single-page runbook + run-level playbook with explicit rollback criteria and escalation matrix.
4) Console dashboard tile and telemetry show rollout progress, per-customer token spend delta, and SLO degradation within 5 minutes of deviation.
5) Run a rehearsal (simulated canary) with oncall and validate rollback sequence before wide rollout.

Scope (in-scope):
- Canary orchestration patterns and guardrails for Dedicated pools (policy definitions and rollout steps).
- Cost backstop thresholds and enforcement hooks (soft stop + escalate + auto-fallback to lower-cost variant).
- One-page runbook + detailed ops playbook (GitHub/Confluence links) and training session for oncall.
- Dashboard and alerting: rollout progress, P50/P95 latency, error rates, token spend delta, and autoscale action logs.

Out of scope:
- Deep kernel/runtime-level batching optimizations (ENG will handle separate change).
- Long-term pricing model changes or customer contracts.

Key deliverables and milestones:
- 2025-05-09: Draft PRD and stakeholder sync (PM/ENG/SRE/Design) - DONE.
- 2025-05-23: Canary gating metric spec (latency/error/spend signals) - OWNER: ENG - target review.
- 2025-06-06: Cost backstop thresholds defined + enforcement API design - OWNER: PM/ENG/SRE.
- 2025-06-27: Runbook + playbook authored and reviewed by SRE/Ops - OWNER: PM.
- 2025-07-11: Dashboard tile + alerting configured in Console staging - OWNER: Console team.
- 2025-07-25: Canary rehearsal executed with oncall and postmortem - OWNER: SRE.
- 2025-08-08: Production gradual rollout begins (wave 1 -> wave 2 -> wave 3) with 2-week observation window - OWNER: PM/SRE/ENG.

Telemetry & Metrics (what we will watch):
- Rollout adoption: % customers moved per wave, time between waves.
- Latency (P50/P95) and error rate delta compared to baseline window.
- Token spend delta per customer (24h rolling) vs baseline.
- Number of automated backstops triggered and how many required manual intervention.
- Mean time to rollback and MTTR for any incident caused by rollout.

Trade-offs and open decisions:
- Aggressiveness of wave sizing: 10/40/100 vs 5/30/65. Larger early waves shorten time-to-value but increase blast radius. Decision: default 10/40/100; experiment small pilot customers at 5% if willing.
- Backstop enforcement mode: soft-throttle + alert vs immediate hard-throttle. Decision: start soft-throttle with auto-fallback to earlier model variant, escalate if repeated triggers.
- Customer opt-in vs opt-out: default to opt-in for early waves to reduce risk; mandate opt-in gating for customers with spend > $X.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Cost backstop false positives cause unnecessary throttles. Mitigation: maintain a paired-stage evaluation window and require two consecutive windows before auto-fallback.
- Risk: Insufficient telemetry granularity. Mitigation: Add short-term high-frequency sampling during waves; instrument token attribution.
- Risk: Cross-region capacity mismatches during wave. Mitigation: Region-aware canary constraints and region-specific rollouts.

Communications plan:
- Week-of-wave launch announcements to customers in pilot cohort; in-product banner and Customer Success outreach.
- Runbook shared on Confluence and pinned to oncall rotation.
- Post-rehearsal retrospective and short executive one-pager for leadership.
